prompt: Predict insurance claims from 60 tabular columns mixing numbers and categories. Accuracy matters most.
tells: 60 tabular columns mixing numbers and categories
why: Boosted trees handle mixed types, missing values and interactions, and usually win on tabular data.
trap: Deep nets rarely beat boosted trees on ordinary tables.

prompt: Churn depends on combinations, like low usage only matters for customers on annual plans. A linear model misses this.
why: Trees capture interactions automatically without you engineering them.
trap: You could hand-craft interaction terms, but trees find them for you.

prompt: You have millions of labeled transactions with 200 features and want the most accurate fraud score possible.
why: With plenty of labels, a supervised boosted model beats unsupervised anomaly detection.
trap: Anomaly detection is for when you lack labels; here you have millions.

prompt: A sensor dataset has many missing values and skewed features, and you'd rather not spend weeks on preprocessing.
tells: many missing values and skewed features
rather not spend weeks on preprocessing
why: Tree ensembles handle missing values and skew natively.
trap: PCA and linear models need careful scaling and imputation first.
